description: Curiosa, analítica e organizada, gosto de transformar dados em histórias claras. Buscamos pessoas que unam rigor técnico e boa comunicação para criar um painel de IA sobre segurança contra incêndio em microgravidade — se isso te interessa, bora construir juntos!
summary: Fire Tamers is an educational dashboard designed to make scientific data from the PSI-159 studies, Advanced Combustion Through Microgravity Experiments / Cool Flames Investigation with Gases, accessible and understandable to the general public, especially high school students. The project was developed by collecting, organizing, and structuring combustion-related experimental data into visual representations that help users explore different aspects of the experiments, identify patterns, and better understand the behavior of flames under microgravity conditions. By transforming complex research data into accessible information, the dashboard helps users interpret experimental results, understand combustion phenomena under microgravity conditions, and engage with scientific discoveries beyond traditional classroom materials. Fire Tamers aims to bridge the gap between scientific research and public understanding, breaking the barriers that often make advanced knowledge inaccessible. We believe that making space science more approachable can inspire curiosity, strengthen scientific literacy, and encourage the next generation to explore science, technology, and research.
details:
The Challenge: Making Science Truly Accessible

Scientific research generates vast amounts of data that contribute to our understanding of natural phenomena and the development of new technologies. However, access to information does not necessarily mean access to knowledge. Scientific data is often presented in technical formats, accompanied by specialized terminology and experimental relationships that can make it difficult for people without prior knowledge of the subject to interpret.

This barrier becomes even more evident when it comes to space research. Although investigations conducted by NASA represent extraordinary learning opportunities, their findings can seem distant from the everyday experiences of students and the general public.

It was from this perspective that Fire Tamers was born: how can we transform data from a scientific investigation into combustion under microgravity into an experience that anyone interested in science can explore, understand, and learn from?

Our Solution: Transforming Data into Knowledge

Fire Tamers was developed to bring scientific research closer to the public through an interactive platform for exploration and learning, using data from the PSI-159 investigation as its foundation.

Rather than simply making experimental information available, our goal is to provide users with the resources they need to understand what they are observing. To achieve this, the data is organized and presented through an interactive dashboard featuring filters, charts, visual representations, and analytical insights. These tools allow users to explore different aspects of the experiments, identify patterns, and establish relationships between the information.

The platform also provides explanations of the scientific phenomena being studied and incorporates an artificial intelligence feature that allows users to search for concepts, clarify questions, and deepen their understanding directly while navigating the platform.

In this way, users do not need to approach the platform with advanced knowledge of combustion or microgravity experiments. They can start with curiosity and progressively build their understanding.

Learning Beyond Data

We understand that scientific understanding does not come solely from observing charts or reading information. For this reason, Fire Tamers incorporates different resources that make the experience more visual, dynamic, and engaging.

Among these resources are three-dimensional (3D) simulations, which allow users to visually explore phenomena related to the experiments, bringing abstract scientific concepts closer to more intuitive representations.

Additionally, the platform features short educational quizzes that allow users to test their knowledge and assess what they have learned throughout their exploration.

The combination of these resources offers different ways to interact with science: observing, investigating, questioning, visualizing, and testing knowledge. In this way, Fire Tamers transforms access to scientific data into an active learning experience.

Impact: Democratizing Scientific Knowledge

The impact we aim to achieve goes beyond making data from a specific investigation available. Our goal is to contribute to the democratization of scientific knowledge, making research and discoveries more accessible to people who often lack the opportunities or tools to explore them.

We believe science should not only be publicly available, but also understandable. When data is presented without context, explanations, or relationships that allow it to be interpreted, much of its educational potential remains unexplored.

By reducing the gap between researchers, students, and society, we hope to encourage scientific interest, strengthen scientific literacy, and expand the number of people capable of interpreting information, asking questions, and developing their own understanding of scientific phenomena.

Our purpose is to spark curiosity that can grow into knowledge, and knowledge that can give rise to new researchers, professionals, and science enthusiasts.

Creativity and Approach

What makes Fire Tamers distinctive is its integration of science, technology, and education into a single environment. Rather than limiting the experience to data visualization, we developed a platform that combines information exploration, AI-assisted explanations, three-dimensional simulations, and learning activities.

This approach recognizes that different people learn in different ways and that engagement with scientific research can begin even without specialized prior knowledge.

By using real data from a NASA investigation as our starting point, we aim to bring students closer to scientific practice, showing that research does not have to remain restricted to academic papers or specialized environments: it can also be explored, questioned, and understood through interactive digital experiences.
